title: Compactification comparison normalizes bounded etale-origin transposes
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], with chosen compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and $\dim\overline X\leq D$ for an integer $D\geq0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Neither $X$ nor $Y$ is required to be separated over $k$. On ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], $F_e=Rp_{e,*}j_!^e$, $F_p=Rp_{p,*}j_!^p$ for compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and $f^\times$ for the right adjoint of $F_e$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Use $Rf^!=C_Xf^\times R\nu_{Y,*}$ with the bounded etale-origin adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Define
$$B_{f,J}=Rp_{p,*}(e_{j,J})\circ\beta_{p,j_!^eJ}:C_YF_eJ\xrightarrow{\sim}F_pC_XJ$$
from the counit-mate proper comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and adjoint extension-by-zero comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Explicitly, the phrase “chosen-compactification normalization” fixes the Hom bijection as follows; it is not an arbitrary adjunction structure on these functors. Put $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$ and let $\eta_T,\tau_T$ be the unit and counit of $C_T\dashv U_T$. For $G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the specified bijection sends $z:F_pC_XG\to L$ to
$$\Phi_{G,L}(z)=C_X\!\left(\operatorname{adj}_e\left(U_Y(z\circ B_{f,G})\circ\eta_{Y,F_eG}\right)\right).$$
Here $\operatorname{adj}_e$ has target $\operatorname{Hom}(G,f^\times U_YL)$; the last operation is the fully faithful comparison at $X$. This spells out the bounded etale-origin Hom-chain construction, using the identity witness and the same compactification $c$ throughout.
Let $J\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $f^\times K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The comparison unit $K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{Y,*}C_YK$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] induces
$$\rho_K:C_Xf^\times K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!C_YK.$$
For the etale counit $\varepsilon^e_K:F_ef^\times K\to K$, its image under $C_Y$, precomposed by $B_{f,f^\times K}^{-1}$, is the bounded etale-origin counit followed by the identification $\rho_K^{-1}$ on the right-adjoint object. Equivalently,
$$\varepsilon^p_{C_YK}\circ F_p(\rho_K)\circ B_{f,f^\times K}=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_K).$$
Consequently, for every $a_e:F_eJ\to K$ and $a_p:F_pC_XJ\to C_YK$ with $a_p B_{f,J}=C_Y(a_e)$, their specified adjunction transposes obey
$$\operatorname{adj}_p(a_p)=\rho_K\circ C_X(\operatorname{adj}_e(a_e)).$$
This comparison uses only the bounded-below etale-origin adjunction, with its chosen-compactification normalization, and is natural in $J,K$. It makes no assertion of an ambient pro-etale exceptional adjunction on all unbounded objects.

proof.text:
For the fixed compactification, $p$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Exactness of $j_!^e$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $j_!^eG$ bounded below whenever $G$ is. Both extension-by-zero functors are exact [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], and $C_T$ is the termwise exact comparison [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Thus the natural sheaf isomorphism $e_j$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] gives a natural isomorphism on complexes: its naturality applied to each differential says precisely that its components are a chain map, and the inverse components give its inverse. It descends to derived categories since these exact functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] to $p$ and $j_!^eG$ and apply the functor $Rp_{p,*}$ to $e_{j,G}$. Their composite is exactly the specified $B_{f,G}$, so it is a natural isomorphism. In particular, for $b:G\to G'$,
$$B_{f,G'}\circ C_Y(F_eb)=F_p(C_Xb)\circ B_{f,G}.$$
This uses the named proper counit-mate and the named open comparison, so introduces no independently chosen compact-support isomorphism.

source.place: Proof: exact open comparison degreewise, followed by the proper direct-image comparison; named-map normalization from Stacks 0B65

proof.text:
Write $H=f^\times$ and $R=C_XHU_Y$. The hypotheses of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] are exactly the field, finite coefficient ring, separated finite-type morphism, compactification and dimension bound in the statement. It supplies $R$ on $D^+$ and the natural relative Hom bijection. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], $C_X$ is fully faithful on $D^+$ and $C_Y\dashv U_Y$ has invertible unit there. The ordinary adjunction $F_e\dashv H$ is supplied by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. With the normalization explicitly fixed in the statement, the bijection is the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_pC_XG,L)\xrightarrow{z\mapsto zB_{f,G}}\operatorname{Hom}(C_YF_eG,L)\xrightarrow{w\mapsto U_Y(w)\eta_{Y,F_eG}}\operatorname{Hom}(F_eG,U_YL)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{adj}_e}\operatorname{Hom}(G,HU_YL)\xrightarrow{C_X}\operatorname{Hom}(C_XG,RL).$$
Every displayed arrow is bijective. The first is Step 1; the middle arrows are the two cited adjunctions; the last is full faithfulness. To check the last domain, exactness gives $\mathcal H^i(RL)=C_X\mathcal H^i(HU_YL)$ [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Full faithfulness on degree-zero sheaves reflects zero: if $C_XM=0$, its identity has zero image, hence $1_M=0$. Since $RL$ is bounded below by the class theorem, $HU_YL$ is therefore bounded below, as is $G$. These are precisely its bounded etale-origin domains, without a separatedness assumption on $X$ or $Y$ over $k$.

source.place: Displayed bounded-below Hom chain; its chosen-compactification normalization is expanded in the statement

proof.text:
For $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ put $G=HU_YL$ in Step 2. The inverse image of $1_{RL}=C_X(1_{HU_YL})$ in that chain is, successively, $1_{HU_YL}$, the etale counit $\varepsilon^e_{U_YL}$, then $\tau_{Y,L}\circ C_Y(\varepsilon^e_{U_YL})$, and finally
$$\varepsilon^p_L=\tau_{Y,L}\circ C_Y(\varepsilon^e_{U_YL})\circ B_{f,HU_YL}^{-1}.$$
These inverse formulas follow directly from an adjunction: the inverse transpose of $b:G\to HV$ is $\varepsilon^e_V\circ F_e(b)$, and the inverse comparison transpose of $a:M\to U_YL$ is $\tau_{Y,L}\circ C_Y(a)$. Thus the displayed map is the specified relative counit, not just some map between the same objects. Here $G$ is bounded below by Step 2 and $RL=C_XG$ has its identity etale-origin witness.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, proof: counit corresponds to identity; inverse adjunction formulas

proof.text:
Let $L=C_YK$ and $h=H(\eta_{Y,K})$. The comparison unit is a natural isomorphism on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], so $\rho_K=C_Xh$ is a natural isomorphism. Both $HK$ and $HU_YC_YK$ lie in $D^+$, the first by the hypothesis $f^\times K\in D^+$ and the second by Step 2. Step 1 gives
$$B_{f,HU_YC_YK}^{-1}\circ F_p(\rho_K)\circ B_{f,HK}=C_Y(F_eh).$$
Substituting this into Step 3 and then using naturality of the etale counit gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^p_{C_YK}\circ F_p(\rho_K)\circ B_{f,HK}
&=\tau_{Y,C_YK}\circ C_Y(\varepsilon^e_{U_YC_YK}\circ F_eH(\eta_{Y,K}))\\
&=\tau_{Y,C_YK}\circ C_Y(\eta_{Y,K})\circ C_Y(\varepsilon^e_K)\\
&=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_K).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the left triangle identity for $C_Y\dashv U_Y$. This proves the required normalization with its specified direction of $B$ and $\rho$.

source.place: Tag 0B65, counit normalization, expanded using naturality and the comparison triangle identity

proof.text:
Given $a_e,a_p$ as in the statement, set $b_e=\operatorname{adj}_e(a_e)$, so $\varepsilon^e_K\circ F_e(b_e)=a_e$. Let $b_p=\rho_K\circ C_X(b_e)$. Naturality of $B$ at $b_e:J\to HK$ and Step 4 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^p_{C_YK}\circ F_p(b_p)\circ B_{f,J}
&=\varepsilon^p_{C_YK}\circ F_p(\rho_K)\circ B_{f,HK}\circ C_Y(F_e(b_e))\\
&=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_K\circ F_e(b_e))=C_Y(a_e)=a_p\circ B_{f,J}.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel the isomorphism $B_{f,J}$. By naturality in the source of the Hom bijection in Step 2, its inverse sends $b_p:C_XJ\to RC_YK$ to $\varepsilon^p_{C_YK}\circ F_p(b_p)$: apply source naturality to the identity of $RC_YK$, whose inverse image defines the counit in Step 3. Injectivity of that inverse bijection therefore gives $\operatorname{adj}_p(a_p)=b_p$, as required. This argument only uses sources $C_XJ$ and $RC_YK$ that are bounded below and of etale origin.

source.place: Tag 0B65, proof: the natural Hom map determines the mate; application of the normalized counit equation

proof.text:
Naturality in $J$ follows by precomposing each of the Hom-chain maps in Step 2; naturality in $K$ follows by postcomposition in that chain and the naturality of $\eta_Y$. More explicitly, for $u:J'\to J$, both transposes precompose by $C_Xu$, and for $v:K\to K'$ they postcompose by $RC_Yv$ and $C_XHv$, respectively, with
$$RC_Y(v)\circ\rho_K=\rho_{K'}\circ C_X(Hv).$$
The latter equality is $C_XH$ applied to $U_YC_Y(v)\eta_{Y,K}=\eta_{Y,K'}v$. Thus the comparison of transposes is natural in both variables on the stated domains. All constructions used one chosen compactification and the specified Hom bijections, so no assertion about an unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjunction has entered.
